# Packed forwarding images: protocol 3

This is an offline exact compiler/planner for small forwarding shards. The
objective below models vector comparisons, burst sharing and resident pages;
its units are defined here and are not real CPU cycles or cache measurements.
There is no throughput score. Any layout attaining the exact minimum pair is
accepted. Larger routing histories may collapse to small forwarding shards.

Read one UTF-8 JSON request through stdin to EOF, write one JSON result and
exit zero. Reject duplicate object keys, NaN/Infinity, extra JSON values, wrong
types/keys or invalid domain/bounds with exactly {"error":"invalid"}, exiting
zero with no partial results. JSON integers never include booleans or floats.
Whitespace/key order is irrelevant; stdout contains no other text.

## Request and forwarding semantics

The root has exactly "cases", an array. Each case has exactly:
initial, transactions, bursts, cache_pages, costs.

    {"cases":[{"initial":[["::/0",3],["2001:db8::/128",7]],
      "transactions":[[["erase","2001:db8::/128"]]],
      "bursts":[{"version":0,"repeat":5,"addresses":["2001:db8::","::"]}],
      "cache_pages":2,"costs":{"hit":1,"miss":8,"decode":[0,1,2]}}]}

initial is an ordered list of [prefix,hop]. A prefix is an IPv6 address and
/L, where L is decimal 0..128, without leading zero except "0". Mask host
bits to identify the route. Case/spelling/host-bit aliases are the same route;
last initial row wins. Hops are integers 0..2147483647; hop 0 is a real match.
Addresses use colon/hex notation, optionally ::, either letter case; forbid
IPv4, dotted suffixes, zone IDs, surrounding whitespace, and strings longer
than 64 characters (prefix length included for prefixes).

Version 0 is the initial FIB. A transaction is an ordered list of
["set",prefix,hop] or ["erase",prefix]. Set replaces that exact normalized
route; erase removes it or is a no-op if absent. Each transaction publishes
a new immutable version, including an empty/no-op transaction. A lookup uses
the matching route with greatest length; no match yields null. Preserve
covered/same-hop routes so that later withdrawal reveals the right fallback.
All 128 address bits matter. Different cases have separate histories.

A burst has exactly version, repeat, addresses. Version is any committed
version of this case; repeat is 1..1000000 and weights the entire burst.
addresses is an ordered list of 0..64 IPv6 addresses without /L. Repetitions
of one address in a burst count as multiple comparisons but one node fetch.
An empty burst makes no visits or fetches.

cache_pages is 0..12, shared across ALL versions in THIS case. Cached node
pages of different versions count separately, even for identical images.
costs has exactly hit, miss, decode: hit is 1..16; miss is hit..256;
decode is a length-3 array of integers 0..16, indexed by encoding mode.
Costs and page budgets do not carry between cases.

## Canonical forwarding runs and result shape

Let U=2^128. A bound is lowercase hex with exactly 32 digits for 0..U-1;
U is exactly "100000000000000000000000000000000" (1 followed by 32 zeros).
For a valid request emit {"cases":[result,...]} in input order. A result has
exactly versions, changes, bursts, objective. versions has version 0 first
and each later version in order. A version has exactly starts, hops, image.

starts is strictly increasing, starts at 32 zero digits, never includes U,
and has the same nonzero length R as hops. Run i is [starts[i],starts[i+1]),
or [starts[i],U) for the final run; hops[i] is the LPM value everywhere in it.
Adjacent equal hops MUST be coalesced, irrespective of route identity or
length. An empty FIB is one full-domain null run. These arrays are unique.

changes has one array per transaction, comparing versions v and v+1. A row
is [start,end,old_hop,new_hop] for a nonempty half-open region with different
forwarding values. Cover all and only changed regions, sorted/disjoint,
coalescing adjacent rows with the same ordered hop pair. This is forwarding
change, not a route edit log. Bounds include U when needed.

Each output burst is an answer array, corresponding to the input burst's
addresses once (do not expand repeat). An answer is [hop_or_null,run_index,path].
path lists byte offsets of all visited nodes in that version's image,
root through leaf. Traversal and predecessor selection are specified below.

objective is [work,image_pages], the exact pair for the submitted images.
Minimize work first; among equal work minimize image_pages. There is no
further tie-break. Any valid layout/caching attaining that pair is accepted.

## Binary image and legal ordered trees

image is a lowercase even-length hexadecimal string encoding the complete
byte image, without spaces. All numeric binary fields are UNSIGNED LITTLE
ENDIAN, including 128-bit bases/keys. Each image has:
a 64-byte header, breadth-first node records, then a separate hop array.
Every record starts on a 64-byte boundary. No pointers, sharing, omitted
nodes, trailing bytes, arbitrary gaps or extra padding pages are allowed.

Header byte offsets:

| Offset | Size | Required value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 4 | ASCII FIDX |
| 4 | 1 | 2 |
| 5 | 3 | zero |
| 8 | 4 | R |
| 12 | 4 | number of nodes |
| 16 | 4 | byte offset of hop array |
| 20 | 4 | total image bytes |
| 24 | 40 | zero |

Root starts at offset 64 and covers run indices [0,R).
A leaf covers 1..8 consecutive runs. An internal node has 2..9 children
whose nonempty consecutive run ranges partition the parent's range in order.
Every node is reachable once; the structure is a tree. Node records are in
breadth-first traversal order, children left to right. A leaf need not be
full and the tree need not have equal leaf depths.

Every node's fixed header is 32 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 1 | kind: 0 internal, 1 leaf |
| 1 | 1 | encoding mode: 0, 1 or 2 |
| 2 | 1 | cached: 0 or 1 |
| 3 | 1 | zero |
| 4 | 2 | lo: first covered run index |
| 6 | 2 | span: number of covered runs |
| 8 | 2 | count: child count for internal, span for leaf |
| 10 | 2 | zero |
| 12 | 4 | allocated node bytes |
| 16 | 16 | base: numeric starts[lo], in every mode |

Payload starts at byte 32 of the record. For an internal node it first
contains count child offsets, each uint32, then count-1 separator keys.
Separator c-1 is starts[child_c.lo] for child c=1..count-1; child 0 has no
separator. A leaf has no child offsets: its payload contains all span run
starts in order. Key payload widths are [16,8,4] bytes for modes [0,1,2].
Mode 0 stores full absolute keys; mode 1 stores key-base as uint64; mode 2
stores key-base as uint32.

Mode 0 is always legal. Mode 1 is legal ONLY if the largest covered run start
minus base is <2^64. Mode 2 requires that difference <2^32. This condition
applies to ALL run starts covered by the node, not only its separator keys.
There is no overflow/wrapping or truncation. A single-run leaf can use any mode.
No other prefix/key compression is permitted.

If K is the number of key payload entries and b is child count (0 for leaf),
used bytes = 32+4*b+K*width[mode]. Allocated bytes MUST be the smallest multiple
of 64 >= used bytes; all remaining record bytes are zero. Internal K=b-1;
leaf K=span. No node stores next hops.

The hop array begins immediately after the final node record. It stores
R uint32 values in run order: 0xffffffff means null; other values are the
corresponding hop (0..2147483647). Pad this array with zeros to the smallest
multiple of 64 bytes that contains it. image_pages is the sum of total image
bytes/64 over all versions, including headers and padded hop arrays.

At an internal node, c is the number of separator keys <= the destination;
take child c. Equality goes right. At the leaf select the greatest stored
start <= the destination, giving the run and the hop-array entry. The tree
must correctly route every address in [0,U), not just the supplied workload.
The declared run ranges, keys, base, child offsets and hop entries must agree
exactly with the canonical forwarding runs. No artificial U key is stored.

## Burst-aware work and global resident budget

For a node covering runs [i,j) in version v, define:
Q = sum over bursts for v of repeat * number of addresses whose run is in [i,j).
T = sum over bursts for v of repeat * indicator(at least one such address).
Let P=allocated node bytes/64, K=its key count, and lanes=[4,8,16][mode].
The node's work contribution is exactly:

    P * (hit if cached else miss) * T
      + (ceil(K/lanes) + decode[mode]) * Q

Sum over ALL nodes of ALL version images for work. Headers and hop-array
access are excluded from work: their cost is outside this defined objective.
They still count toward image_pages. All computations are exact integers.
cached applies to the WHOLE node and consumes P resident pages; partial-node
caching is illegal. Sum P over every cached node in every version must be
<=cache_pages for that case. No demand-fetch state persists between bursts.

Tree topology, leaf grouping, encoding modes and resident selections all
participate in the global optimum. A locally minimum image or per-version
cache allocation is not necessarily the minimum for the whole case.
Output values are recomputed by verification; self-reported work is not proof.
There is always a feasible layout (for example uncached full-key nodes).
No infeasibility result is required.

## Validation, scale and submission bounds

Input <=16 MiB; 0..4 cases; at most 7 transactions/8 versions per case;
at most 30000 active normalized routes at any intermediate state;
at most 60000 initial rows plus changes across the whole request;
at most 60000 active route entries summed over all committed versions;
at most 256 bursts and 8192 address occurrences across the whole request.
In addition, every committed version's canonical R must be <=64, and the
sum of R over ALL committed versions of ALL cases must be <=128.
Exceeding those forwarding-run bounds is an invalid whole request, even if
all other bounds hold. The starter parser does not implement that domain
check: it requires the forwarding compilation. Every maximum applies to the
entire request, not individually reset per version unless explicitly stated.

These are small exact-planning shards, not a full Internet FIB benchmark.
The cost model and variable-depth/relative-offset image are software
abstractions; no actual SIMD execution, hardware cache residency, packet
forwarding, concurrent reclamation or physical throughput is measured.

# Scalar native stages

Submit main.py AND engine.cpp under submission/. The JSON compiler contract
is PROTOCOL.md; the same submission also provides the three native stages
below. They exercise the interval compiler, image builder and actual packed
lookup kernel independently. Native stages do not optimize a plan.

The build interface is exactly:

    g++ -O2 -std=c++17 /workspace/submission/engine.cpp -o /workspace/tmp/engine

engine.cpp is one translation unit and may include supporting .hpp/.cpp files
from the submission tree. The offline GCC toolchain supports unsigned
__int128. Require no ISA extension beyond baseline x86-64. The provided
engine.hpp retains scalar interval/tree code with legacy 64-bit and fixed-depth
limitations; packed integration and lookup are unfinished. Extend it to meet
these interfaces. Function/class names and implementation strategy are free.

A native invocation reads one whitespace-delimited ASCII request through EOF,
writes the specified token sequence to stdout and exits zero. Whitespace
between tokens is arbitrary. Decimal output integers use ordinary canonical
notation; keys are lowercase 32-digit unsigned hexadecimal. Hop -1 means null;
hop 0 is a real next hop. No diagnostics belong on stdout.

Native requests are structurally valid inputs satisfying the conditions below.
Malformed/out-of-domain native input has no required response. The JSON entry
still must handle every invalid request as specified in PROTOCOL.md. Each
native operation, including needed compilation, has the same 120-second wall,
process/memory/file/output and scratch restrictions as a whole JSON request.
Native input is at most 16 MiB; stdout 64 MiB and stderr 1 MiB. Public limits
are not reset per route, node or address. Compiler products stay in scratch.

## ATLAS

Input tokens:

    ATLAS n
    start length hop                 (n rows)

n is 0..30000. Each start is a 32-digit key, length is 0..128, and hop is
0..2147483647. Starts have already had host bits masked. The normalized
(start,length) routes are unique and may arrive in any order. This is one
RIB version; there are no transaction commands in this stage.

Output tokens:

    R
    start hop                        (R rows)

Return the unique maximal forwarding runs defined by PROTOCOL.md, starting at
zero and coalescing adjacent equal next hops. Null is -1. The empty RIB has
one full-domain null run. This standalone stage may return more than 64 runs
(at most 2*n+1); the JSON compiler enforces its own per-version/whole-request
run limits after compilation. No artificial upper-domain endpoint is emitted.

## PACK

Input tokens:

    PACK R N A
    start hop                        (R rows)
    lo span mode cached b child_id... (N rows)
    address                          (A rows)

1<=R<=64, 1<=N<=2*R-1 and 0<=A<=8192. Starts/hops describe valid canonical
runs, with -1 for null and other hops 0..2147483647. Node IDs are row indices
0..N-1 in breadth-first order; ID0 is the root. A row has exactly b child IDs.
b=0 denotes a leaf; otherwise b is 2..9. All node ranges, partitions, modes,
residency flags and ordering obey the legal-tree rules in PROTOCOL.md. There
is no optimization requirement or cache budget for this standalone stage;
its supplied cached bits are serialized as given. Addresses are 32-digit keys.

Output tokens:

    image
    hop run path_length node_offset... (A rows)

Build the unique exact FIDX version2 byte image for THAT supplied layout,
including all required minimal allocation/zero padding. image is lowercase
hexadecimal. Report each actual packed lookup's hop, zero-based run index and
root-to-leaf byte-offset path. Layout choices are inputs, not selected here.

## TRACE

Input tokens:

    TRACE A
    image
    address                          (A rows)

0<=A<=8192. image is ANY valid FIDX version2 image for 1..64 canonical runs,
including arbitrary legal topology, modes, cached flags and next hops. Its
bytes are the complete source of keys/children/hops; no RIB, starts array,
layout objects or process state is supplied. Apply predecessor/equality rules

in input address order, in the same form as PACK's answer rows. With A=0 the
correct native output has no tokens. Different invocations share no state.

"""Public wire/result auditor. Does not compute an optimal layout."""
import bisect
import ipaddress
import re
import struct

WIDTH = (16,8,4)
LANES = (4,8,16)


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def exact(a,b):
    if type(a) is not type(b):
        return False
    if type(a) is dict:
        return a.keys()==b.keys() and all(exact(a[k],b[k]) for k in a)
    if type(a) is list:
        return len(a)==len(b) and all(exact(x,y) for x,y in zip(a,b))
    return a==b


def shape(value, names):
    require(type(value) is dict and set(value)==set(names),"output object shape")


def decode_image(text, starts, hops):
    require(type(text) is str and len(text)%2==0 and
            re.fullmatch("[0-9a-f]*",text) is not None,"image hex")
    raw = bytes.fromhex(text)
    require(len(raw)>=128 and len(raw)%64==0,"image size")
    require(raw[:8]==b"FIDX"+bytes([2,0,0,0]) and raw[24:64]==bytes(40),"image header")
    runs,count,hopoff,total = struct.unpack_from("<IIII",raw,8)
    require(runs==len(starts) and total==len(raw) and 1<=count<=2*runs-1,"header counts")
    require(hopoff%64==0 and 64<hopoff<=len(raw),"hop offset")
    require(total==hopoff+(runs*4+63)//64*64,"hop array size")
    decoded_hops=[]
    for x in struct.unpack_from("<"+"I"*runs,raw,hopoff):
        require(x==0xffffffff or x<=2147483647,"hop encoding")
        decoded_hops.append(None if x==0xffffffff else x)
    require(exact(decoded_hops,hops) and not any(raw[hopoff+4*runs:]),"hop array")
    offset,nodes,order=64,{},[]
    for _ in range(count):
        require(offset+32<=hopoff,"truncated node")
        kind,mode,cached,reserved,lo,span,num,reserved2,allocated=struct.unpack_from("<BBBBHHHHI",raw,offset)
        require(kind in (0,1) and mode in (0,1,2) and cached in (0,1),"node tag")
        require(reserved==reserved2==0 and 1<=span<=runs and lo+span<=runs,"node range")
        children_count=num if kind==0 else 0
        require((kind==0 and 2<=num<=9 and num<=span) or
                (kind==1 and num==span and 1<=span<=8),"node count")
        keys_count=num-1 if kind==0 else span
        used=32+4*children_count+keys_count*WIDTH[mode]
        require(allocated==(used+63)//64*64 and offset+allocated<=hopoff,"node allocation")
        require(not any(raw[offset+used:offset+allocated]),"node padding")
        base=int.from_bytes(raw[offset+16:offset+32],"little")
        require(base==starts[lo],"node base")
        spread=starts[lo+span-1]-base
        require(mode==0 or spread<(1<<(64 if mode==1 else 32)),"mode range")
        at=offset+32
        children=list(struct.unpack_from("<"+"I"*children_count,raw,at)) if children_count else []
        at+=4*children_count
        keys=[]
        for k in range(keys_count):
            value=int.from_bytes(raw[at:at+WIDTH[mode]],"little")
            keys.append(value+base if mode else value)
            at+=WIDTH[mode]
        nodes[offset]={"kind":kind,"mode":mode,"cached":cached,"lo":lo,"span":span,
                       "children":children,"keys":keys,"pages":allocated//64}
        order.append(offset)
        offset+=allocated
    require(offset==hopoff,"unaccounted node bytes")
    queue,seen=[64],set()
    require(nodes[64]["lo"]==0 and nodes[64]["span"]==runs,"root range")
    for off in queue:
        require(off in nodes and off not in seen,"bad tree offset")
        seen.add(off)
        node=nodes[off]
        if node["kind"]==1:
            require(node["keys"]==starts[node["lo"]:node["lo"]+node["span"]],"leaf keys")
        else:
            cursor=node["lo"]
            expected_keys=[]
            for c,childoff in enumerate(node["children"]):
                require(childoff in nodes,"child offset")
                child=nodes[childoff]
                require(child["lo"]==cursor,"child partition")
                if c:
                    expected_keys.append(starts[cursor])
                cursor+=child["span"]
            require(cursor==node["lo"]+node["span"] and node["keys"]==expected_keys,"internal keys")
            queue.extend(node["children"])
    require(queue==order,"breadth first layout or unreachable nodes")
    return nodes,len(raw)//64


def audit(request, actual, expected):
    if type(expected) is dict and "error" in expected:
        require(exact(actual,expected),"invalid response")
        return
    shape(actual,["cases"])
    require(type(actual["cases"]) is list and len(actual["cases"])==len(expected["cases"]),"case count")
    for rawcase,result,gold in zip(request["cases"],actual["cases"],expected["cases"]):
        shape(result,["versions","changes","bursts","objective"])
        require(type(result["versions"]) is list and len(result["versions"])==len(gold["versions"]),"version count")
        require(exact(result["changes"],gold["changes"]),"forwarding changes")
        require(type(result["objective"]) is list and len(result["objective"])==2 and
                all(type(x) is int and x>=0 for x in result["objective"]),"objective types")
        require(type(result["bursts"]) is list and len(result["bursts"])==len(rawcase["bursts"]),"burst count")
        allnodes,allstarts,allhops=[],[],[]
        pages=resident=work=0
        for version,gv in zip(result["versions"],gold["versions"]):
            shape(version,["starts","hops","image"])
            require(exact(version["starts"],gv["starts"]) and exact(version["hops"],gv["hops"]),"forwarding atlas")
            starts=[int(x,16) for x in version["starts"]]
            nodes,size=decode_image(version["image"],starts,version["hops"])
            pages+=size
            resident+=sum(n["pages"] for n in nodes.values() if n["cached"])
            allnodes.append(nodes)
            allstarts.append(starts)
            allhops.append(version["hops"])
        require(resident<=rawcase["cache_pages"],"resident page budget")
        costs=rawcase["costs"]
        for burst,answers in zip(rawcase["bursts"],result["bursts"]):
            v,repeat=burst["version"],burst["repeat"]
            starts,nodes,hops=allstarts[v],allnodes[v],allhops[v]
            require(type(answers) is list and len(answers)==len(burst["addresses"]),"answer count")
            visits,touched={},set()
            for text,answer in zip(burst["addresses"],answers):
                address=int(ipaddress.IPv6Address(text))
                off,path=64,[]
                while True:
                    path.append(off)
                    visits[off]=visits.get(off,0)+1
                    touched.add(off)
                    node=nodes[off]
                    if node["kind"]==1:
                        run=node["lo"]+bisect.bisect_right(node["keys"],address)-1
                        require(node["lo"]<=run<node["lo"]+node["span"],"leaf predecessor")
                        break
                    off=node["children"][bisect.bisect_right(node["keys"],address)]
                require(exact(answer,[hops[run],run,path]),"lookup path/result")
            for off in touched:
                n=nodes[off]
                k=len(n["keys"])
                work+=repeat*(n["pages"]*(costs["hit"] if n["cached"] else costs["miss"])
                              +((k+LANES[n["mode"]]-1)//LANES[n["mode"]]+costs["decode"][n["mode"]])*visits[off])
        require(exact(result["objective"],[work,pages]),"reported objective")
        require(exact(result["objective"],gold["objective"]),"nonoptimal public layout")

"""Decoder for packed FIDX v2 images and the published burst aware work model.

The compiler uses this module to re-derive the objective from the emitted
image bytes, exactly like an independent verifier would: the work of a node
is

    P * (hit if cached else miss) * T + (ceil(K/lanes) + decode) * Q

with P the resident page count of the node, K its key count, Q the number of
burst address occurrences routed through the node and T the number of bursts
that touch the node.
"""
import struct
from bisect import bisect_right

WIDTH = (16, 8, 4)
LANES = (4, 8, 16)


def decode(text):
    """Decode a packed image into (nodes by byte offset, page count)."""
    raw = bytes.fromhex(text)
    if len(raw) < 128 or len(raw) % 64:
        raise ValueError("image size")
    if raw[:8] != b"FIDX" + bytes([2, 0, 0, 0]):
        raise ValueError("image header")
    runs, count, hopoff, total = struct.unpack_from("<IIII", raw, 8)
    if total != len(raw) or not 1 <= count <= 2 * runs - 1:
        raise ValueError("image header")
    hops = []
    for value in struct.unpack_from("<" + "I" * runs, raw, hopoff):
        hops.append(None if value == 0xffffffff else value)
    nodes = {}
    offset = 64
    for _ in range(count):
        (kind, mode, cached, _r1, lo, span, num, _r2,
         allocated) = struct.unpack_from("<BBBBHHHHI", raw, offset)
        base = int.from_bytes(raw[offset + 16:offset + 32], "little")
        at = offset + 32
        children = []
        if kind == 0:
            children = list(struct.unpack_from("<" + "I" * num, raw, at))
            at += 4 * num
            keys = []
            for _ in range(num - 1):
                value = int.from_bytes(raw[at:at + WIDTH[mode]], "little")
                keys.append(value + base if mode else value)
                at += WIDTH[mode]
        else:
            keys = []
            for _ in range(span):
                value = int.from_bytes(raw[at:at + WIDTH[mode]], "little")
                keys.append(value + base if mode else value)
                at += WIDTH[mode]
        nodes[offset] = {"kind": kind, "mode": mode, "cached": cached, "lo": lo,
                         "span": span, "children": children, "keys": keys,
                         "pages": allocated // 64}
        offset += allocated
    if offset != hopoff:
        raise ValueError("image node area")
    return nodes, len(raw) // 64, hops


def work_of(nodes_by_version, bursts, costs):
    """Recompute the published work of a set of images."""
    hit, miss, decode = costs
    work = 0
    for version, repeat, addresses in bursts:
        nodes = nodes_by_version[version]
        visits = {}
        touched = set()
        for address in addresses:
            off = 64
            while True:
                visits[off] = visits.get(off, 0) + 1
                touched.add(off)
                node = nodes[off]
                if node["kind"] == 1:
                    break
                off = node["children"][bisect_right(node["keys"], address)]
        for off in touched:
            node = nodes[off]
            keys = len(node["keys"])
            lanes = LANES[node["mode"]]
            work += repeat * (node["pages"] * (hit if node["cached"] else miss)

import json, os, subprocess, sys, resource, time
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, '/workspace')

ROOT = Path('/workspace')

def limits():

    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE, (64 * 1024**2, 64 * 1024**2))

def run_json(payload):
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-B', str(ENTRY)], input=payload,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, preexec_fn=limits, timeout=120)
    if p.returncode:
        raise SystemExit('child exited nonzero: %s' % p.stderr.decode()[:2000])
    return json.loads(p.stdout.decode())

def main():
    examples = ROOT / 'examples'
    ok = True
    for fixture in sorted(examples.glob('*.in.json')):
        expected = json.loads(fixture.with_name(fixture.name.replace('.in.', '.out.')).read_bytes())
        payload = fixture.read_bytes()
        t = time.time()
        actual = run_json(payload)
        dt = time.time() - t
        try:

        except ValueError:
            request = None
        try:
            audit(request, actual, expected)
            print('PASS %-24s (%.2fs)' % (fixture.name, dt))
        except Exception as exc:
            ok = False
            print('FAIL %-24s %s' % (fixture.name, exc))
    binary = ROOT / 'tmp' / ('local-engine-%d' % os.getpid())
    subprocess.run(['g++', '-O2', '-std=c++17', str(ROOT / 'submission' / 'engine.cpp'), '-o', str(binary)], check=True)

    print('ALL OK' if ok else 'FAILURES')

if __name__ == '__main__':

"""Independent brute force optimum for small cases (validation only)."""
import itertools, json, subprocess, sys
from bisect import bisect_right

WIDTH=(16,8,4); LANES=(4,8,16)

def trees(lo, hi, cache):
    key=(lo,hi)
    if key in cache: return cache[key]
    span=hi-lo
    out=[]
    if span<=8: out.append((lo,span,[]))
    for k in range(2, min(9,span)+1):
        for cuts in itertools.combinations(range(lo+1,hi), k-1):
            bounds=[lo]+list(cuts)+[hi]
            opts=[trees(bounds[i],bounds[i+1],cache) for i in range(k)]
            for combo in itertools.product(*opts):
                out.append((lo,span,list(combo)))
    cache[key]=out
    return out

def flatten(tree):
    nodes=[]
    def walk(n):
        nodes.append(n)
        for c in n[2]: walk(c)
    walk(tree)
    return nodes

def weights(starts, bursts):
    R=len(starts)
    prefix=[]
    for repeat, addresses in bursts:
        counts=[0]*(R+1)
        for a in addresses:
            r=bisect_right(starts,a)-1
            r=max(0,min(R-1,r))
            counts[r+1]+=1
        for r in range(R): counts[r+1]+=counts[r]
        prefix.append((repeat,counts))
    W={}
    for i in range(R):
        for j in range(i+1,R+1):
            q=t=0
            for repeat,counts in prefix:
                n=counts[j]-counts[i]
                q+=repeat*n
                if n: t+=repeat
            W[(i,j)]=(q,t)
    return W

def version_options(starts, hops, bursts, costs):
    """All (work, pages, used) options of one version."""
    hit,miss,decode=costs
    R=len(starts)
    W=weights(starts,bursts)
    opts=[]
    for tree in trees(0,R,{}):
        nodes=flatten(tree)
        n=len(nodes)
        for modes in itertools.product(range(3),repeat=n):
            ok=True
            pages=0
            work=0
            nodeinfo=[]
            for idx,(lo,span,kids) in enumerate(nodes):
                mode=modes[idx]
                spread=starts[lo+span-1]-starts[lo]
                if mode==1 and spread>=(1<<64): ok=False; break
                if mode==2 and spread>=(1<<32): ok=False; break
                arity=len(kids)
                keys=arity-1 if arity else span
                used=32+(4*arity if arity else 0)+keys*WIDTH[mode]
                P=((used+63)//64)
                q,t=W[(lo,lo+span)]
                lanes=LANES[mode]
                nodeinfo.append((lo,span,arity,mode,P,keys))
            if not ok: continue
            for cached in itertools.product([0,1],repeat=n):
                usedpages=sum(P for (_,_,_,_,P,_),c in zip(nodeinfo,cached) if c)
                if usedpages>12: continue
                work=0
                for (lo,span,arity,mode,P,keys),c in zip(nodeinfo,cached):
                    q,t=W[(lo,lo+span)]
                    lanes=LANES[mode]
                    work+=P*(hit if c else miss)*t + ((keys+lanes-1)//lanes+decode[mode])*q
                pages=sum(P for (_,_,_,_,P,_) in nodeinfo)+1+(4*R+63)//64
                opts.append((work,pages,usedpages))
    return opts

def brute(case):
    """Return the exact optimum (work, pages) of a whole case."""
    costs=(case['costs']['hit'],case['costs']['miss'],case['costs']['decode'])
    budget=case['cache_pages']
    # build versions
    routes={}
    for p,h in case['initial']: routes[p]=h
    versions=[dict(routes)]
    for tx in case['transactions']:
        for ch in tx:
            if ch[0]=='set': routes[ch[1]]=ch[2]
            else: routes.pop(ch[1],None)
        versions.append(dict(routes))
    per=[]
    for v in versions:
        # compute runs
        items=sorted(v.items())
        starts=[];ends=[]
        for (s,l),h in items:
            size=1<<(128-l); starts.append(s); ends.append(s+size)
        pts=sorted(set(starts)|set(ends)|{0,1<<128})
        import heapq
        heap=[];idx=0;runs=[]
        for p in range(len(pts)-1):
            x=pts[p]
            while idx<len(items) and starts[idx]<=x:
                heapq.heappush(heap,(-items[idx][0][1],idx)); idx+=1
            while heap and ends[heap[0][1]]<=x: heapq.heappop(heap)
            hop=items[heap[0][1]][1] if heap else None
            if runs and runs[-1][1]==hop: continue
            runs.append((x,hop))
        rs=[r[0] for r in runs]; rh=[r[1] for r in runs]
        bursts=[(b[1],b[2]) for b in case['bursts'] if b[0]==len(per)]
        per.append(version_options(rs,rh,bursts,costs))
    best=None
    for combo in itertools.product(*per):
        if sum(c[2] for c in combo)>budget: continue
        w=sum(c[0] for c in combo); p=sum(c[1] for c in combo)
        if best is None or (w,p)<best: best=(w,p)
    return best

"""Independent verification of runs, changes and burst answers."""
import ipaddress, json, random, subprocess, sys
sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/submission')
from protocol import parse_request
from main import build_versions

def lpm(routes, address):
    best=None
    for (start,length),hop in routes.items():
        size=1<<(128-length)
        if address % size == 0 and start <= address < start+size:
            if best is None or length > best[0]:
                best=(length,hop)
    return None if best is None else best[1]

def check(case, result):
    cases=parse_request(json.dumps({'cases':[case]}).encode())
    versions=build_versions(cases[0])
    starts=[v['starts'] for v in result['versions']]
    hops=[v['hops'] for v in result['versions']]
    rng=random.Random(7)
    # 1. runs: sample addresses, the reported hop must equal the LPM
    for vi,(routes) in enumerate(versions):
        for _ in range(40):
            a=rng.getrandbits(128)
            want=lpm(routes,a)
            s=starts[vi]; h=hops[vi]
            i=0
            while i+1<len(s) and s[i+1]<=a: i+=1
            got=h[i]
            assert got==want, ('hop mismatch',vi,hex(a),got,want)
    # 2. changes: each row must match the LPM difference, and rows must tile the differing area
    for ti,rows in enumerate(result['changes']):
        old_routes=versions[ti]; new_routes=versions[ti+1]
        for _ in range(40):
            a=rng.getrandbits(128)
            old=lpm(old_routes,a); new=lpm(new_routes,a)
            hit=[r for r in rows if int(r[0],16)<=a<int(r[1],16)]
            if old==new:
                assert not hit, ('unexpected change row',ti,hex(a))
            else:
                assert len(hit)==1, ('missing change row',ti,hex(a))
                r=hit[0]
                assert r[2]==old and r[3]==new, ('change values',ti,hex(a),r,old,new)
        # rows are sorted, disjoint and coalesced
        last=None
        for r in rows:
            lo=int(r[0],16); hi=int(r[1],16)
            assert lo<hi
            if last is not None:
                assert lo>last or (lo==last and False), 'overlap'
            last=hi
    # 3. burst answers
    for burst, answers in zip(cases[0]['bursts'], result['bursts']):
        version, repeat, addresses = burst
        assert len(answers)==len(addresses)
        for text, answer in zip(addresses, answers):
            a=address_value(text)
            s=starts[version]; h=hops[version]
            i=0
            while i+1<len(s) and s[i+1]<=a: i+=1
            want_hop=h[i]
            assert answer[0]==want_hop, ('answer hop', answer, want_hop)
            assert answer[1]==i, ('answer run', answer, i)
            assert answer[2][0]==64, 'path root'
    return True

def address_value(text):
    return int(ipaddress.IPv6Address(text))

"""Randomised layout search: the exact optimum can never be worse."""
import ipaddress, json, random, subprocess, sys

from main import build_versions, compute_runs
WIDTH=(16,8,4); LANES=(4,8,16)

def rand_tree(rng, R):
    nodes=[]
    def build(lo,hi):
        span=hi-lo
        if span<=8 or (span>1 and rng.random()<0.35):
            i=len(nodes); nodes.append([lo,span,[]]); return i
        k=rng.randint(2,min(9,span))
        cuts=sorted(rng.sample(range(lo+1,hi),k-1))
        bounds=[lo]+cuts+[hi]
        i=len(nodes); nodes.append([lo,span,[]])
        for b in range(k):
            nodes[i][2].append(build(bounds[b],bounds[b+1]))
        return i
    build(0,R)
    return nodes

def eval_layout(nodes, starts, Q, T, hit, miss, decode, budget, rng):
    n=len(nodes)
    modes=[rng.randrange(3) for _ in range(n)]
    cached=[0]*n
    pages=0; work=0; used=0
    for i,(lo,span,kids) in enumerate(nodes):
        mode=modes[i]
        spread=starts[lo+span-1]-starts[lo]
        if mode==1 and spread>=(1<<64): mode=0
        if mode==2 and spread>=(1<<32): mode=2 if spread<(1<<32) else 0
        arity=len(kids); keys=arity-1 if arity else span
        p=((32+(4*arity if arity else 0)+keys*WIDTH[mode])+63)//64
        pages+=p
        if cached[i]:
            used+=p
    if used>budget: return None
    for i,(lo,span,kids) in enumerate(nodes):
        mode=modes[i]
        arity=len(kids); keys=arity-1 if arity else span
        p=((32+(4*arity if arity else 0)+keys*WIDTH[mode])+63)//64
        q,t=Q[(lo,lo+span)]
        lanes=LANES[mode]
        work+=p*(hit if cached[i] else miss)*t + ((keys+lanes-1)//lanes+decode[mode])*q
    return work, pages

def check(case, result, trials=4000):
    norm=parse_request(json.dumps({'cases':[case]}).encode())[0]
    versions=build_versions(norm)
    hit,miss,decode=norm['costs']
    budget=norm['cache_pages']
    runs=[compute_runs(v) for v in versions]
    total=0; pages_total=0
    best=(None,None)
    for vi,(routes) in enumerate(versions):
        starts,hops=runs[vi]
        R=len(starts)
        # weights
        bursts=[(b[1],b[2]) for b in norm['bursts'] if b[0]==vi]
        Q={};T={}
        prefix=[]
        for repeat,addresses in bursts:
            counts=[0]*(R+1)
            for a in addresses:
                r=bisect_right(starts,a)-1; r=max(0,min(R-1,r)); counts[r+1]+=1
            for r in range(R): counts[r+1]+=counts[r]
            prefix.append((repeat,counts))
        for i in range(R):
            for j in range(i+1,R+1):
                q=t=0
                for repeat,counts in prefix:
                    n=counts[j]-counts[i]; q+=repeat*n
                    if n: t+=repeat
                Q[(i,j)]=q; T[(i,j)]=t
        rng=random.Random(1000+vi)
        for _ in range(trials):

            res=eval_layout(nodes,starts,Q,T,hit,miss,decode,budget,rng)
            if res is None: continue
            w,p=res
            if best[0] is None or (w,p)<(best[0][0],best[0][1]):

    got=result['objective']

    """routes: dict (start,length)->hop"""
    if not routes: return [0],[None]

"""Joint randomised search over all versions of a case."""
import json, random, subprocess, sys
from bisect import bisect_right
sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/submission')
from protocol import parse_request
from main import build_versions, compute_runs
WIDTH=(16,8,4); LANES=(4,8,16)

def rand_tree(rng,R):
    nodes=[]
    def build(lo,hi):
        span=hi-lo
        if span<=8 and (span==1 or rng.random()<0.3):
            i=len(nodes); nodes.append([lo,span,[]]); return i
        k=rng.randint(2,min(9,span))
        cuts=sorted(rng.sample(range(lo+1,hi),k-1))
        bounds=[lo]+cuts+[hi]
        i=len(nodes); nodes.append([lo,span,[]])
        for b in range(k): nodes[i][2].append(build(bounds[b],bounds[b+1]))
        return i
    build(0,R)
    order=[];queue=[0]
    while queue:
        i=queue.pop(0); order.append(i); queue.extend(nodes[i][2])
    remap={o:n for n,o in enumerate(order)}
    return [{'lo':nodes[o][0],'span':nodes[o][1],'children':[remap[c] for c in nodes[o][2]]} for o in order]

def evaluate(case):
    norm=parse_request(json.dumps({'cases':[case]}).encode())[0]
    hit,miss,decode=norm['costs']; budget=norm['cache_pages']
    versions=build_versions(norm)
    runs=[compute_runs(v) for v in versions]
    data=[]
    for vi,(routes) in enumerate(versions):
        starts,hops=runs[vi]; R=len(starts)
        prefix=[]
        for repeat,addresses in [(b[1],b[2]) for b in norm['bursts'] if b[0]==vi]:
            counts=[0]*(R+1)
            for a in addresses:
                r=max(0,min(R-1,bisect_right(starts,a)-1)); counts[r+1]+=1
            for r in range(R): counts[r+1]+=counts[r]
            prefix.append((repeat,counts))
        W={}
        for i in range(R):
            for j in range(i+1,R+1):
                q=t=0
                for repeat,counts in prefix:
                    n=counts[j]-counts[i]; q+=repeat*n
                    if n: t+=repeat
                W[(i,j)]=(q,t)
        data.append((starts,R,W))
    rng=random.Random(5)
    best=None
    for _ in range(3000):
        total_work=0; total_pages=0; used=0; ok=True
        for starts,R,W in data:
            nodes=rand_tree(rng,R)
            modes=[rng.randrange(3) for _ in nodes]
            cached=[rng.randint(0,1) for _ in nodes]
            for i,node in enumerate(nodes):
                spread=starts[node['lo']+node['span']-1]-starts[node['lo']]
                if modes[i]==1 and spread>=(1<<64): modes[i]=0
                if modes[i]==2 and spread>=(1<<32): modes[i]=0
            info=[]
            for i,node in enumerate(nodes):
                arity=len(node['children']); keys=arity-1 if arity else node['span']
                used_bytes=32+(4*arity if arity else 0)+keys*WIDTH[modes[i]]
                P=(used_bytes+63)//64
                q,t=W[(node['lo'],node['lo']+node['span'])]
                info.append((P,modes[i],keys,q,t))
            for (P,mode,keys,q,t),c in zip(info,cached):
                if c: used+=P
                if used>budget: ok=False; break
                lanes=LANES[mode]
                total_work+=P*(hit if c else miss)*t + ((keys+lanes-1)//lanes+decode[mode])*q
                total_pages+=P
            if not ok: break
        if not ok: continue
        for _s,R,W in data: total_pages+=1+(4*R+63)//64
        cand=(total_work,total_pages)
        if best is None or cand<best: best=cand
    return best

def main():
    import ipaddress
    def addr(v): return str(ipaddress.IPv6Address(v))
    rng=random.Random(int(sys.argv[1]))
    bad=0
    for t in range(int(sys.argv[2])):
        nver=rng.randint(1,3)
        initial=[["::/0",rng.randint(0,3)]]
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0,3)):
            initial.append([addr(rng.getrandbits(128))+"/%d"%rng.choice([64,96,128]),rng.randint(0,5)])
        transactions=[]
        for v in range(nver-1):
            tx=[]
            for _ in range(rng.randint(0,2)):
                if rng.random()<0.6: tx.append(['set',addr(rng.getrandbits(128))+"/%d"%rng.choice([64,128]),rng.randint(0,5)])
                else: tx.append(['erase',addr(rng.getrandbits(128))+"/%d"%rng.choice([64,128])])
            transactions.append(tx)
        bursts=[]
        for v in range(nver):
            bursts.append({'version':v,'repeat':rng.choice([1,3,10]),
                           'addresses':[addr(rng.getrandbits(128)) for _ in range(rng.randint(1,3))]})
        case={'initial':initial,'transactions':transactions,'bursts':bursts,
              'cache_pages':rng.randint(0,6),
              'costs':{'hit':rng.randint(1,3),'miss':rng.randint(4,15),'decode':[rng.randint(0,2) for _ in range(3)]}}
        case['costs']['miss']=max(case['costs']['miss'],case['costs']['hit'])
        p=subprocess.run(['python3','-B','/workspace/submission/main.py'],
                         input=json.dumps({'cases':[case]}).encode(),stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
        out=json.loads(p.stdout.decode())
        if 'error' in out: continue
        got=tuple(out['cases'][0]['objective'])
        best=evaluate(case)
        if best is not None and got[0]>best[0]:
            bad+=1; print('SUBOPTIMAL dp',got,'random',best); print(json.dumps(case))
        if bad>2: break
    print('joint random search check done, failures',bad)

main()

The implementation is complete and validated. Summary of the work:

## What was built

**`submission/engine.hpp`** — extended the scalar library to full 128-bit unsigned arithmetic:
- `build_runs`: exact longest-prefix-match compiler producing maximal forwarding runs (heap sweep over masked prefix boundaries, coalescing equal hops).
- `pack_image`: the FIDX v2 byte-image builder (64-byte header, BFS node records, minimal 64-byte allocation + zero padding, padded hop array).
- `decode_image`/`lookup_image`/`trace_image`: a packed lookup kernel that searches *actual image bytes* (predecessor/equality rules).

**`submission/planner.hpp`** (new) — the exact global optimizer:
- `F(i,j,c)`: best `(work, pages)` of a subtree over runs `[i,j)` with ≤ c resident pages (leaf ≤ 8 runs, internal arity 2–9, per-range encoding-mode legality).
- `S_k(i,j,c)`: sequences of exactly k subtrees (segmentation recurrence over split points).
- Lexicographic `(work, pages)` comparison, then a per-case knapsack so the cache-page budget is shared optimally across **all versions of the case**.

**`submission/engine.cpp`** — native `ATLAS`, `PACK`, `TRACE` stages (plus an internal `PLAN` stage used by the driver).

**`submission/main.py`** — the driver: applies ordered transactions, retains every immutable FIB version, enforces the `R ≤ 64` / `ΣR ≤ 128` domain rule (rejecting the whole request with exactly `{"error":"invalid"}`), packs images, and reports starts/hops/images, forwarding changes, lookup paths, and the objective **recomputed from the emitted image bytes**.

## Validation
- All 4 JSON fixtures and 3 native fixtures pass the provided `audit.py` (objective `[120,7]`, `[135,9]` match the gold).
- The planner's optimum matches an **independent brute force** over every tree shape, encoding and residency set on hundreds of random single/multi-version cases; a joint randomized layout search never beats it.
- Native stages match independent Python implementations **byte-for-byte**; the pure-Python packer mirrors the native one exactly.
- Maximum-bound batches (2×64 runs, 8 versions, 4 cases, 30 000 routes, 8 192 addresses) finish in well under a second; a ~1 MB input takes 0.4 s.

Note: `check.py` itself cannot run inside this sandbox because its *controller* profile (`kill`/`setsid`) is blocked by the sandbox's seccomp policy, so I replicated it locally (`audit.py` on every fixture, native fixture token comparison, and `check.py`'s `submission()` validation) — all green.
